title: Asking the right question: what the user did, not what they thought

videos.script: Every ticket arrives with an explanation attached. The printer is broken. The internet is down. I didn't touch anything. {{attached}} The person means every word, and some of it is wrong, because they are describing what they think happened, not what they did. {{means}} This lesson is about the questions that get you from one to the other: questions about actions and times, asked without blame. {{questions}} And about one trap on your side of the call: testing as yourself, seeing it work, and deciding the user must be mistaken. {{trap}}
